document_metadata.title: Sales Team State-to-State Route Requirements
document_metadata.intended_use: Web-app copy and document checklist for sales representatives before approving a dealer transaction
document_metadata.important_scope_note: This is an operational sales-tax documentation tool, not legal or tax advice. Registration duties, nexus, local taxes, contractor use, installation, rentals, and product-specific rules can change the result. Escalate incomplete, inconsistent, or unusual facts to the company's tax adviser.

step_shape.title: Short action heading
step_shape.purpose_label: Very short plain-English reason for the step, such as “Proof that they sold it”
step_shape.downloads: Array of actionable forms or app assets; empty when no download is needed

download_object_shape.url: HTTPS source when available; null for an app asset
download_object_shape.asset_key: Present only when access_type is app_asset
download_object_shape.button_label: Display label for the form button

frontend_rules: Render all three steps in order, including a not_required informational step.
Use is_edge_case and edge_cases for route-specific callouts; do not infer edge cases from state names.
Render purpose_label as the step's short plain-English why label, not as a separate section.
Render step downloads as form buttons inside that step.
Do not add separate summaries, document bubbles, customer-document lists, release checklists, or stop-condition sections.
The step title and instruction are the single source of truth for what the sales representative must collect.

1.title: Direct drop shipment
1.definition: The manufacturer ships directly to the dealer's customer, and the dealer does not hold the delivery state's registration.

2.title: Connecticut pickup with dealer-controlled shipping
2.definition: The order is made available at the Connecticut facility, and the dealer or dealer-hired carrier takes possession there and controls outbound transportation.

3.title: Direct drop shipment using the dealer's delivery-state registration
3.definition: The manufacturer ships directly to the dealer's customer, and the dealer already holds the delivery state's registration.

edge_case_catalog.no_statewide_sales_tax_delivery: Delivery to Delaware, Montana, New Hampshire, or Oregon: no statewide resale form is required.
edge_case_catalog.no_home_state_resale_permit: Dealer home state does not issue a normal statewide resale permit; collect the named business proof and FEIN instead.
edge_case_catalog.alaska_local_tax_review: Alaska requires an address-specific local/ARSSTC review.
edge_case_catalog.local_jurisdiction_review: A home-rule locality may require separate documentation.
edge_case_catalog.ct_registered_dealer: A Connecticut dealer supplies its Connecticut permit and must not sign a permit-not-required statement.

route.title: Direct drop shipment using the dealer's delivery-state registration

steps.title: Collect an accepted Alabama resale form
steps.purpose_label: Proof that we can ship it
steps.instruction: Ask the dealer to complete Alabama Form ST:EX-A1 or MTC Uniform Sales & Use Tax Resale Certificate — Multijurisdiction before shipment. The dealer must use its Alabama Sales Tax License details, describe the equipment as inventory for resale, and sign and date the form.

downloads.official_name: Alabama Form ST:EX-A1
MTC Uniform Sales & Use Tax Resale Certificate — Multijurisdiction

steps.title: Collect the dealer's Alabama registration proof
steps.purpose_label: Proof that they can sell it
steps.instruction: Ask for a current copy of the dealer's Alabama Sales Tax License. Make sure the dealer's legal name and registration number match the Alabama form collected in Step 1.

steps.title: Collect proof of the dealer's sale to the end customer
steps.purpose_label: Proof that they sold it
steps.instruction: Before shipment, ask for the signed end-customer purchase order, sales contract, or dealer quote acceptance showing the same equipment and the Alabama ship-to customer. Add the dealer's final invoice to the end customer as soon as it is issued.

steps.title: Collect a Connecticut resale certificate
steps.purpose_label: Proof that we can sell it for resale
steps.instruction: First ask whether the dealer already has a completed MTC Multijurisdiction Certificate issued for resale. If yes, collect it. If not, send the Connecticut Sales and Use Tax Resale Certificate. The dealer must enter the registration number from its Alabama Sales Tax License, describe the equipment, and sign and date the form before pickup.

downloads.official_name: Connecticut Sales and Use Tax Resale Certificate
MTC Uniform Sales & Use Tax Resale Certificate — Multijurisdiction

steps.title: Collect the dealer's Alabama registration proof
steps.purpose_label: Proof that they can sell it
steps.instruction: Ask for a current copy of the dealer's Alabama Sales Tax License. Make sure the dealer's legal name and registration number match the Connecticut resale form collected in Step 1.

steps.title: Collect the signed Connecticut permit-not-required statement
steps.purpose_label: Proof that no Connecticut permit is needed
steps.instruction: Send the Connecticut Permit Not Required Statement to the dealer. The dealer must confirm that it is not making Connecticut sales or other sales that require a Connecticut Sales and Use Tax Permit, then sign and return the statement before pickup.

downloads.official_name: Connecticut Permit Not Required Statement

edge_cases.label: Edge case — Alaska local-tax review

steps.title: Collect the dealer's existing MTC certificate
steps.purpose_label: Proof that we can ship it
steps.instruction: Ask the dealer to provide a completed MTC Multijurisdiction Certificate that it already has before shipment. Do not ask the dealer to create a new MTC certificate for this sale. If it does not already have one, use Option 2 instead. Make sure the document identifies Alabama as the home jurisdiction, uses the registration number from the dealer's Alabama Sales Tax License, covers the equipment as inventory for resale, and is signed and dated. Do not accept an Alabama document by itself for delivery to Arizona.

steps.instruction: Before shipment, ask for the signed end-customer purchase order, sales contract, or dealer quote acceptance showing the same equipment and the North Dakota ship-to customer. Add the dealer's final invoice to the end customer as soon as it is issued.

steps.instruction: Ask for a current copy of the dealer's Wyoming Sales/Use Tax License. Make sure the dealer's legal name and registration number match the South Dakota form collected in Step 1.

steps.title: Collect proof of the dealer's sale to the end customer
steps.purpose_label: Proof that they sold it
steps.instruction: Before shipment, ask for the signed end-customer purchase order, sales contract, or dealer quote acceptance showing the same equipment and the South Dakota ship-to customer. Add the dealer's final invoice to the end customer as soon as it is issued.

steps.title: Collect the dealer's existing MTC certificate
steps.purpose_label: Proof that we can ship it
steps.instruction: Ask the dealer to provide a completed MTC Multijurisdiction Certificate that it already has before shipment. Do not ask the dealer to create a new MTC certificate for this sale. If it does not already have one, use Option 2 instead. Make sure the document identifies Wyoming as the home jurisdiction, uses the registration number from the dealer's Wyoming Sales/Use Tax License, covers the equipment as inventory for resale, and is signed and dated. Do not accept a Wyoming document by itself for delivery to Tennessee.
